text:
Priya (Sec): FYI customer on Dedicated wants to bring their FIPS HSM. Found a vendor firmware vuln (CVSS ~7.3) in their model. Asking how this affects BYOK custody, RBAC for support, and our audit retention obligations.
Mateo (SRE): Are they asking us to provision a proxy HSM or to mount their HSM into our rack? Need clarity on network topology first.
Jin (CS): They want a physically separate HSM in their VPC with a TLS-only proxy to our control plane. They emphasized dual-control (operator + custodian) and no vendor remote access.
Hana (Product): Important to confirm whether we will ever see unwrapped key material. We must enforce envelope encryption if keys are customer-managed.
Alex (Eng): Agree. Technical constraints: if we do envelope encryption, we only store ciphertext and metadata. That reduces blast radius but has implications for latency and key rotation flows.
Priya (Sec): On RBAC: customer requests that our oncall engineers be able to trigger failover and rewrap operations but not see key material. Suggest creating two entitlements: support.action (can call rewrap/failover) + support.view-meta (can see logs/ops metadata). No read-key permission.
secbot: Automated note: existing role "support:engineer" currently has datastore:read privileges. Recommend audit before change.
Nora (Compliance): Retention note: SOC2 requires immutable audit trails for key operations; PCI wants detailed key management logs for five years in some cases. We need to confirm customer's regulatory profile (HIPAA? PCI?).
Jin (CS): Customer is PCI scope and also GDPR data controller for EU tenants. They want logs retained in their region and not exported.
Mateo (SRE): Practical ask: how long do we keep authz decisions, operator identity, and rewrap diffs? We can keep detailed traces for 7 years but storage/ingress costs and residency matter.
Priya (Sec): Minimum: 1) authz decision + principal ID + action + object + result + request_id 2) before/after metadata for rewraps (no key material) 3) KMS envelope IDs and thumbprints 4) KMS client certs used. Retention period configurable per-customer, default 2 years, can be extended on contract.
Alex (Eng): Firmware vuln: if vendor pushes patch that requires HSM reboot, we need a playbook for safe rewrap order and TTL of KV cache. Propose automated canary: replicate to staging HSM, run rewrap, verify integrity, then schedule maintenance.
Hana (Product): Also need to document SLA impact and customer notification windows. For Dedicated customers, maintenance windows must be agreed.
Priya (Sec): Incident triage steps (high level): 1) Confirm vuln advisory + exploitability 2) Assess if private keys or wrapping keys are affected 3) If wrap keys at risk -> immediate emergency rewrap to fallback KMS 4) Notify legal/compliance and customer with TLP:AMBER
Mateo (SRE): Add-on: ensure KV cache invalidation across all serving nodes within 30s of rewrap; otherwise old tokenized ciphertext might be served. That needs a cluster-wide pub/sub invalidation event.
Alex (Eng): Pseudocode for rewrap orchestration we discussed:
```
start_rewrap(request_id):
  lock(customer_id)
  for each partition in parallel:
    fetch_envelope_ids()
    rewrap_to_target_kms()
    emit_audit(request_id, principal, before_hash, after_hash)
  unlock(customer_id)
  publish_invalidation(request_id)
```
Make sure logs do not contain plaintext.
Jin (CS): Customer insisted on split-ops: their custodian initiates, our operator executes. Need an approval workflow (signed container or out-of-band OTP).
Priya (Sec): For split-control we can implement a 2-step API: initiate_rewrap(token_signed_by_custodian) then execute_rewrap(by operator principal). Token should be bound to TTL and replay-protected.
Nora (Compliance): eDiscovery/regulatory: exportable audit evidence must be tamper-evident (immutable hashes). Recommend append-only object store + periodic Merkle snapshots we can hand to auditors.
secbot: Checklist generated: [RBAC delta, Audit retention policy, Rewrap playbook, KV invalidation PR, Customer contract scoping].
Hana (Product): Who owns the RBAC delta PR?
Alex (Eng): I'll draft RBAC changes: new roles support.action + support.meta + rewrap.operator. Will add unit tests ensuring no write/read key APIs are exposed. ETA 48h.
Mateo (SRE): I'll prototype the invalidation pub/sub and measure 95th percentile invalidation time. ETA 2 days.
Priya (Sec): I'll coordinate incident playbook for firmware vuln, draft customer-facing notification template, and check vendor attestation requirements. ETA EOD tomorrow.
Nora (Compliance): I'll draft audit retention amendments for PCI/GDPR and confirm region-locked storage options with legal. ETA 3 business days.
Jin (CS): I'll ask customer to sign POA for split-control and confirm maintenance windows.
Priya (Sec): Action items summarized: @Alex (RBAC PR), @Mateo (invalidation), @Priya (playbook & notif), @Nora (retention/legal), @Jin (customer POA). Please update the thread when you have PR link or docs.
Alex (Eng): Noted. Will link PR here once created.
Mateo (SRE): Will spin up a staging HSM and run simulated rewrap; will log timings.
Jin (CS): Customer asked: do we accept vendor HSM firmware updates during maintenance or do they manage it? Answer: we require customer sign-off; we can coordinate but vendor access must be via customer's channel.
Priya (Sec): Final: no changes to key custody boundaries — we never expose unwrapped key material. All operations are envelope-based. Any exception requires a written security waiver. :white_check_mark:
